questions.name: List Management
questions.text: A bookkeeper wants to see all the available lists in QuickBooks Online from a single menu. According to the Student Guide, which navigation path opens the All Lists screen?

answers.text: Click the Gear icon → All Lists
Click +New → All Lists
Click Reports → All Lists
Click Banking → All Lists

explanations.a: Correct — All Lists is accessed from the Gear icon menu under the Lists column.
explanations.b: The +New menu creates new transactions, not navigates to lists.
explanations.c: Reports opens the Report Center, not the All Lists screen.
explanations.d: Banking opens the Banking Center for bank feeds, not the lists menu.

questions.name: List Management
questions.objective: 3.2 Customer list access from left nav
questions.text: According to the Student Guide, where is the Customer Center located in the QuickBooks Online left navigation bar?

answers.text: Banking → Customers
Sales → Customers
+New → Customers
Workers → Customers

explanations.a: Banking opens the Banking Center for downloaded transactions, not the Customer list.
explanations.b: Correct — the Customer Center is opened by clicking Sales in the left navigation bar and then the Customers sub-tab.
explanations.c: +New is for creating new transactions, not navigating to lists.
explanations.d: Workers opens the Employee Center, not the Customer Center.

questions.name: List Management
questions.text: A bookkeeper needs to open the Vendor Center to review outstanding bills and edit vendor contact information. According to the Student Guide, which left-navigation tab opens the Vendor Center?

answers.text: Banking
Sales
Expenses
Workers

explanations.a: Banking opens the Banking Center for bank feeds.
explanations.b: Sales opens the Customer Center, not the Vendor Center.
explanations.c: Correct — clicking Expenses in the left navigation bar and then the Vendors sub-tab opens the Vendor Center.
explanations.d: Workers opens the Employee Center.

questions.name: List Management
questions.text: According to the Student Guide, which left-navigation tab opens the Employee Center in QuickBooks Online?

answers.text: Sales (left navigation)
Expenses (left navigation)
Banking (left navigation)
Workers (left navigation)

explanations.a: Sales opens the Customer Center.
explanations.b: Expenses opens the Vendor Center.
explanations.c: Banking opens the Banking Center for downloaded bank transactions.
explanations.d: Correct — clicking Workers in the left navigation bar opens the Employee Center, where employees, contractors, and Workers' Comp sub-tabs are accessed.

questions.name: List Management
questions.objective: 3.5 Number of lists in All Lists
questions.text: A new ProAdvisor opens the All Lists screen via the Gear icon to review which lists are available in QuickBooks Online. Which of the following is NOT a list type that appears on the All Lists screen?

answers.text: General Journal Entries
Recurring Transactions
Products and Services
Custom Form Styles

explanations.a: Correct — Journal Entries are transactions, not a list. The All Lists screen does not include a "General Journal Entries" list.
explanations.b: Recurring Transactions is one of the lists on the All Lists screen.
explanations.c: Products and Services is one of the core lists on the All Lists screen.
explanations.d: Custom Form Styles is one of the lists on the All Lists screen used to customize sales forms.

questions.name: List Management
questions.text: A bookkeeper sets up a sub-customer in QuickBooks Online. According to the Student Guide, what billing options are available when creating a sub-customer?

answers.text: Bill the sub-customer separately only — combined billing with the parent is not supported
Choose to bill with the parent customer or bill the sub-customer separately
Bill only the parent — sub-customer transactions automatically roll up
Sub-customers cannot have transactions of their own

explanations.a: Combined billing IS supported — the bookkeeper can choose to bill with the parent.
explanations.b: Correct — when creating a sub-customer, the user checks the Is sub-customer box, selects a parent, and chooses whether to bill with the parent or the sub-customer separately.
explanations.c: Sub-customers can have their own transactions and be billed independently.
explanations.d: Sub-customers can absolutely have their own transactions; that is one of their main purposes.

questions.name: List Management
questions.text: According to the Student Guide, how many levels deep can sub-customers be nested in QuickBooks Online (counting the parent level)?

answers.text: 3 levels
4 levels
5 levels
Unlimited levels

explanations.a: Sub-customers can go deeper than 3 levels.
explanations.b: Sub-customers can go deeper than 4 levels.
explanations.c: Correct — the Student Guide states sub-customers can go up to 5 levels deep including the parent customer (so a parent, sub, sub-sub, sub-sub-sub, sub-sub-sub-sub).
explanations.d: There is a hard limit of 5 levels, not unlimited.

questions.name: List Management
questions.text: On the Chart of Accounts, sub-accounts can be created beneath parent accounts to provide additional detail in financial reporting. According to the Student Guide, how many levels deep can sub-accounts be nested?

answers.text: Unlimited levels deep
3 levels deep
4 levels deep
5 levels including the parent account

explanations.a: Sub-accounts have a hard limit; they are not unlimited.
explanations.b: Sub-accounts can go deeper than 3 levels.
explanations.c: Sub-accounts can go deeper than 4 levels.
explanations.d: Correct — the Student Guide states sub-accounts can go up to 5 levels deep, including the parent account.

questions.name: List Management
questions.text: A bookkeeper finds two duplicate vendor names cluttering the Vendor List. According to the Student Guide, what is the correct procedure to merge them into a single record?

answers.text: Edit the name to be eliminated, change its Display Name to exactly match the surviving name, click Save, and confirm Yes when prompted to merge
Right-click one of the duplicate names and choose Merge with… from the context menu
Delete one of the duplicate names — QuickBooks will automatically reassign its transactions to the remaining name
Open the Reconcile screen to find duplicates and use the Merge tool there

explanations.a: Correct — to merge two list names, edit the one to be eliminated, change its Display Name to exactly match the surviving name, click Save, and click Yes on the confirmation prompt.
explanations.b: There is no right-click "Merge with…" context menu in QuickBooks Online; merging is done via the Edit / Display Name technique.
explanations.c: Deleting a name does NOT merge its transactions; merging is done by matching Display Names exactly.
explanations.d: The Reconcile screen is for bank reconciliations, not for merging list duplicates.

questions.name: List Management
questions.text: According to the Student Guide, what extra step is required when merging a subitem (such as a sub-customer or sub-account) with another list name?

answers.text: No extra step is required — subitems merge using the same Display Name procedure as parent items
The subitem must first be promoted to a parent (top-level) item before being merged; it can then be re-nested as a subitem afterward if desired
Subitems cannot be merged in QuickBooks Online — only parent items can
A QuickBooks Online Plus or Advanced subscription is required to merge subitems

explanations.a: Subitems specifically require an extra step beyond the standard merge procedure.
explanations.b: Correct — to merge a subitem, the user must first remove its sub-item designation (promote it to a parent), perform the merge, and then re-nest it as a subitem if desired.
explanations.c: Subitems CAN be merged; they just require the promotion step first.
explanations.d: Merging is not gated by subscription level; the procedure works on any QBO subscription.

questions.name: List Management
questions.text: After merging two duplicate customer names in QuickBooks Online, a bookkeeper checks the Customer List and is unsure what happened to the eliminated name and its transactions. According to the Student Guide, what actually happens when two list names are merged?

answers.text: The eliminated name and all of its transactions are permanently deleted from the system
The eliminated name remains active in the Customer List with its transactions intact, separate from the surviving name
The eliminated name is made inactive (not deleted), and all of its transactions are reassigned to the surviving name
The eliminated name remains active but its transactions are moved to an Unassigned holding category

explanations.a: The eliminated name is NOT deleted — it is made inactive, and its transactions are reassigned, not deleted.
explanations.b: The eliminated name does NOT remain active after merging.
explanations.c: Correct — per the Student Guide, the merged (eliminated) name is made inactive (not deleted), and all transactions assigned to it are reassigned to the surviving name.
explanations.d: There is no Unassigned holding category for transactions during merge; all transactions move to the surviving name.

questions.name: List Management
questions.objective: 3.12 Deleted list name appearance on reports
questions.keyword: deleted list name inactive history reports
questions.text: A controller deletes an old vendor from the Vendor List but later runs a report covering a prior period. The old vendor still appears on the report. According to the Student Guide, why is this the expected behavior?

answers.text: The vendor was not actually deleted — the controller must delete it again
Reports in QuickBooks Online cache deleted names for 90 days before they disappear
The vendor was reactivated automatically when the report was generated
A deleted list name still appears on reports if it was used in a transaction during the report's reporting period — names are made inactive on deletion, not erased from history

explanations.a: The vendor was correctly deleted; running it again would not change the report behavior.
explanations.b: There is no 90-day cache; the explanation is that deletion makes a name inactive, not erased.
explanations.c: List names are not auto-reactivated by report generation.
explanations.d: Correct — the Student Guide states deleted list names are not actually erased; they are made inactive. Any transactions historically using the name still display the name in reports covering that period.

questions.name: List Management
questions.keyword: reactivate inactive list include inactive make active
questions.text: A bookkeeper accidentally made a customer inactive and now needs to bring them back. According to the Student Guide, what is the correct procedure to reactivate an inactive list name?

answers.text: Open the list center, click the small Gear icon at the top right of the list, check the Include inactive box, click the inactive name, then click Make Active
Open the deleted name from the Audit Log and click Restore Name
Re-create the list name as a new entry — once deleted, list names cannot be reactivated
Contact Intuit Support to manually restore deleted list names from a backup

explanations.a: Correct — per the Student Guide, reactivate an inactive list name by opening the list center, clicking the small Gear icon at the top right, checking Include inactive, clicking the inactive name, and clicking Make Active.
explanations.b: The Audit Log shows historical actions but does not have a "Restore Name" function for list reactivation.
explanations.c: Inactive (deleted) list names CAN be reactivated; they are not permanently erased.
explanations.d: Reactivation is a self-service action that does not require Intuit Support.

questions.name: List Management
questions.objective: 3.14 Including inactive items on a list
questions.text: A bookkeeper opens the Customer Center and only sees a few customers, even though many more should exist. According to the Student Guide, what is the most likely cause and the correct way to display all customers, including inactive ones?

answers.text: The customers were permanently deleted; they cannot be displayed without a backup restore
Many customers are inactive — click the small Gear icon at the top right of the Customer Center and check the Include inactive box to display them
A QuickBooks Online Advanced subscription is required to see inactive customers in the list
Inactive customers can only be displayed by running the Customer Balance Detail report

explanations.a: QBO does not permanently delete list names; they are made inactive and can always be displayed.
explanations.b: Correct — the small Gear icon at the top right of any list center has an Include inactive option that will show inactive list names alongside active ones.
explanations.c: Showing inactive items is available on every QBO subscription, not gated to Advanced.
explanations.d: The Include inactive option works directly on the list center; reports are a separate matter.

questions.name: List Management
questions.objective: 3.15 Default Chart of Accounts behavior at setup
questions.keyword: chart of accounts default industry-based setup
questions.text: When a brand-new QuickBooks Online company is created (without importing from QuickBooks Desktop), what determines the default Chart of Accounts that is initially set up?

answers.text: The user manually creates every account from a blank Chart of Accounts
QuickBooks Online uses a fixed COA template for all companies regardless of industry
QuickBooks Online generates a default Chart of Accounts based on the industry the user selects during setup
The Chart of Accounts is imported from a generic IRS Schedule C template

explanations.a: QBO does provide a default; the user does not start from a blank Chart of Accounts.
explanations.b: The default is industry-specific, not a single fixed template.
explanations.c: Correct — the Student Guide states that when a new QBO company is set up (without importing from Desktop), QuickBooks Online creates a Chart of Accounts based on the industry the user chooses.
explanations.d: The default COA is generated from QBO industry templates, not from an IRS Schedule C template.

questions.name: List Management
questions.text: A bookkeeper exploring the All Lists screen on a QuickBooks Online Plus subscription notices that one specific list type is not available, but is available in QuickBooks Online Advanced. According to the Student Guide, which list type is exclusive to QuickBooks Online Advanced?

answers.text: Recurring Transactions (a list type, not a product/service type)
Locations
Classes
Custom Fields

explanations.a: Recurring Transactions is available in Essentials, Plus, and Advanced.
explanations.b: Locations is available in Plus and Advanced.
explanations.c: Classes is available in Plus and Advanced.
explanations.d: Correct — the Student Guide lists Custom Fields as a list type that is only in QuickBooks Online Advanced; Plus and lower do not have a separate Custom Fields list (though Plus and lower can still create up to 3 custom sales-form fields).

questions.name: List Management
questions.keyword: products services four types inventory non-inventory service bundle
questions.text: When creating a new Product or Service in QuickBooks Online, the user is asked to choose the type. According to the Student Guide, which list correctly names ALL FOUR types available?

answers.text: Inventory, Non-inventory, Service, and Bundle
Inventory, Service, Material, and Labor
Inventory, Asset, Service, and Project
Stock, Non-stock, Service, and Kit

explanations.a: Correct — the Student Guide lists exactly four product/service types: Inventory (Plus/Advanced only, FIFO valuation, tracks quantities), Non-inventory (buy/sell but no quantity tracking), Service (services rendered), and Bundle (group of items sold together).
explanations.b: Material and Labor are not QBO product/service types; the four types are Inventory, Non-inventory, Service, and Bundle.
explanations.c: Asset and Project are not Product/Service types; the four types are Inventory, Non-inventory, Service, and Bundle.
explanations.d: Stock/Non-stock/Kit are terms from other accounting systems; QBO uses Inventory, Non-inventory, Service, and Bundle.

questions.name: List Management
questions.keyword: inventory tracking activation sales products services setting
questions.text: A QuickBooks Online Plus subscriber wants to start tracking inventory in QBO. According to the Student Guide, what specific setting must be enabled, and where is it found?

answers.text: Sales tax tracking under Gear icon → Account and Settings → Sales
Track inventory quantity on hand under Gear icon → Account and Settings → Sales → Products and Services
Inventory module under Gear icon → Account and Settings → Advanced → Categories
Inventory tracking is automatic on Plus and Advanced subscriptions and does not need to be activated

explanations.a: Sales tax is a separate setting and not the inventory toggle.
explanations.b: Correct — per the Student Guide, inventory tracking is enabled under Gear icon → Account and Settings → Sales → Products and Services → Track inventory quantity on hand. It is only available in Plus and Advanced.
explanations.c: Categories is for product categorization, not for activating inventory tracking; the toggle is in the Sales section.
explanations.d: Inventory tracking IS available in Plus and Advanced, but it must be turned on explicitly via the setting; it is not automatic.

questions.name: List Management
questions.text: A new ProAdvisor reviewing inventory features in QuickBooks Online needs to know how QBO values inventory. According to the Student Guide, which inventory valuation method does QuickBooks Online use?

answers.text: Weighted average cost (the same method used by all QuickBooks Desktop editions except Enterprise with Advanced Inventory)
LIFO (Last In, First Out)
FIFO (First In, First Out)
Specific identification (each item tracked individually by serial number)

explanations.a: Weighted average cost is what QuickBooks Desktop uses (except Enterprise with Advanced Inventory). QBO does NOT use weighted average.
explanations.b: LIFO is not supported by QBO at all.
explanations.c: Correct — the Student Guide states that QuickBooks Online values inventory using the FIFO (First In, First Out) method. The only Desktop edition that offers FIFO is Enterprise with Advanced Inventory.
explanations.d: QBO does not use specific identification; it uses FIFO.

questions.name: List Management
questions.keyword: two-sided items sales purchasing plus advanced
questions.text: A QuickBooks Online Plus user wants to track both the cost (when purchased from a vendor) and the income (when sold to a customer) of a single product on a single item record. According to the Student Guide, what specific feature enables this and on which subscription levels is it available?

answers.text: Class Tracking — available on Plus and Advanced
Project Profitability — available on Plus and Advanced
Bundle Items — available on all subscription levels
Two-sided items (mapping both Sales information and Purchasing information on the same product/service record), available on Plus and Advanced only

explanations.a: Class Tracking categorizes transactions by class but does not link cost and income on the same product record.
explanations.b: Project Profitability tracks profitability by project, not at the product level.
explanations.c: Bundles are groups of products sold together but are not the two-sided cost/income mapping feature.
explanations.d: Correct — per the Student Guide, two-sided items let you check both "I sell this product/service to my customers" and "I purchase this product/service from a vendor" on a single item record, mapping it to an income account on sales and an expense (or COGS) account on purchases. This is available only in Plus and Advanced.
